verdict.rationale: Unity documents multiple official programmatic surfaces for agent-driven control: public scripting APIs for editor extension/custom inspectors/property editing (unity-docs-10/11/12/13), CLI/command-line automation for builds and headless CI (unity-docs-6/7/8/9/25/26/28, unity-probe-rt-4), and a first-party MCP server explicitly built for LLM agents like Claude Code/Cursor to create assets, automate workflows, and perform project actions (unity-docs-23/24, unity-probe-4, unity-probe-rt-1). The newer standalone CLI also ships its own fully-supported MCP mode and direct 'unity eval' commands to drive the Editor without MCP overhead (unity-probe-rt-4), and community adoption (14k-star third-party MCP) corroborates real-world agent-editor integration (unity-probe-rt-1). Missing for 10: no public/open MCP server repo (closed distribution requiring package install), and no evidence of a single unified doc showing end-to-end scene/node creation via MCP tools specifically (only asset/workflow/performance actions named).
